item.title: Langfuse Releases Agent Skills for AI Coding Assistants
item.description:
Langfuse Releases Agent Skills for AI Coding Assistants

Agent Skills for Langfuse have been released as an open-source toolkit that teaches AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor how to work with Langfuse, the open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, prompt management, and evaluation.

🧩 What are Agent Skills?

  • Skills are capabilities that enable AI coding assistants to interact with Langfuse
  • They teach assistants to query and manage traces, prompts, datasets, and scores via the Langfuse API
  • They help look up documentation and apply best practices

🔍 Main Skill

  • The primary skill works with Langfuse to handle core operations through the API
  • It supports looking up documentation and applying best practices in mind

🔄 Migration Support

  • The skills include functionality to migrate from other LLM observability platforms (LangSmith, Arize, Braintrust, etc.) to Langfuse
  • The migration process interviews users about scope
  • It handles live tracing cutover and transfers historical traces, datasets, prompts, and evaluators

⚙️ Installation Options

  • Install as a Cursor plugin: /add-plugin langfuse
  • Install via the skills CLI: npx skills add langfuse/skills --skill "langfuse"
  • Clone the repo and symlink: git clone https://github.com/langfuse/skills.git /path/to/langfuse-skills and ln -s /path/to/langfuse-skills/skills/langfuse /path/to/skills-directory/langfuse

🔑 Requirements

  • A Langfuse account (cloud at cloud.langfuse.com, us.cloud.langfuse.com, or self-hosted)
  • API keys: LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL
  • API keys are found in Langfuse project under Settings > API Keys

🚀 Automatic Usage

  • The agent automatically uses these skills when relevant, including:
    • Setting up Langfuse tracing in a project
    • Setting up CI/CD experiment gates with langfuse/experiment-action
    • Auditing existing instrumentation
    • Preparing an application and Langfuse project for the v4 platform migration
    • Migrating prompts to Langfuse prompt management
    • Querying traces, prompts, or datasets via the API
    • Looking up Langfuse docs, SDK usage, or integration guides

💡 Getting Involved

  • Want to improve a skill or add a new one? See CONTRIBUTING.md
  • For issues or new skill requests, start a discussion on GitHub

#Langfuse #AI #LLM #Observability #Evals #CodingAssistants

Source: langfuse/skills

item.title: Workshop teaches building local AI coding agents in Go
item.description:
Workshop teaches building local AI coding agents in Go

A new workshop is available that guides developers through the process of building their own AI-powered coding assistant. The course is designed for those who want to create tools similar to Roo code, Cline, Amp, Cursor, Windsurf, or OpenCode without requiring prior expertise in artificial intelligence. Participants build six progressive versions of a coding assistant, starting from a basic chatbot and ending with a powerful local developer assistant equipped with tool-use capabilities.

🧩 How it works

The core of the agent is described as the event loop, which functions like the agent’s heartbeat. This loop manages the interaction between the user and the AI model:

  • Waits for user input.
  • Sends the input to Claude.
  • Claude either responds directly or requests the use of a tool.
  • The agent executes the requested tool (e.g., reading a file).
  • The result is sent back to Claude.
  • Claude provides the final answer.

As the workshop progresses, the agent acquires specific capabilities through tool integration:

  • File Reading: Allows Claude to read files from the user’s computer and look around the directory.
  • Shell Execution: Permits Claude to run safe terminal commands.
  • Code Modification: Enables Claude to modify code, create files, and make changes.
  • Pattern Search: Utilizes ripgrep to power code searching features.

⚙️ Key details

The workshop requires specific environment configurations to proceed. Tools are conceptualized as plugins that extend the agent’s functionality. Before starting, users must verify their setup using the following criteria:

Requirement Detail
Language Version Go 1.24.2 or later
Shell Environment Use devenv shell to avoid configuration problems
API Verification Check quota on Anthropic’s dashboard
Environment Variable Ensure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported via echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

💡 Why it matters

This resource lowers the barrier to entry for building autonomous coding agents. By following a step-by-step approach, users can construct a functional local assistant capable of interacting with their development environment directly, bridging the gap between simple chatbots and complex, tool-using AI systems.

#AIagents #Claude #GoLanguage #CodingAssistants #Workshop

Source: ghuntley/how-to-build-a-coding-agent

item.title: Context Engine launches AI skills for semantic code search and memory
item.description:
Context Engine launches AI skills for semantic code search and memory

🆕 Overview

Context Engine has launched a suite of AI agent skills designed to teach coding assistants how to utilize 30+ MCP tools for semantic search, symbol graph navigation, and memory. The tool provides semantic code search, memory, and symbol intelligence specifically for AI coding assistants.

🧩 How it works

The Context Engine MCP server indexes workspaces, allowing agents to call repo_search first for any question about the codebase before using standard commands like ls, find, Grep, or Read. Results from repo_search are verified source with exact line ranges, which agents are instructed to treat as already read.

The system includes specific tools for different coding tasks:

  • repo_search: Finds code by behavior, concept, error text, or identifier; supports multiple queries and narrowing by language, path, or type.
  • context_answer: Explains how or why something works across several files with citations.
  • symbol_graph: Shows definitions, callers, callees, importers, and references for specific symbols.
  • graph_query: Performs multi-hop impact analysis before making changes.
  • cross_repo_search: Identifies code that may exist in other indexed repositories.

For safety and efficiency, the system recommends fetching every involved symbol in one call before editing. For renames or signature changes, symbol_graph with query_type=references is used to get every site.

⚙️ Key details

The tool supports various development environments through specific installation and configuration methods:

  • Claude Code & Codex: Recommends pasting guidance into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md to reach subagents. Codex can install natively using its built-in skill installer, which pulls .codex/skills/context-engine/ into ~/.codex/skills/ automatically.
  • Cursor: Rules are included in .cursorrules at the workspace root, which Cursor picks up automatically if the file is present.
  • Terminal-based MCP clients: An MCP bridge allows connection without VS Code for clients like Claude Code or Codex.
  • Daemon Management: The system runs as a background daemon with a default file watch interval of 30 seconds. Users can authenticate, index codebases, and monitor changes. The daemon and MCP server share authentication via ~/.ctxce/auth.json, and logs are stored at ~/.context-engine/daemon.log.
  • Installation: Native installation is available from the public GitHub repo, which pulls the skill and auto-loads MCP tool guidance into the session.

🚀 Availability

Users can get a free account at dev.context-engine.ai.

#AI #CodingAssistants #MCP #SemanticSearch #DeveloperTools

Source: Context-Engine-AI/Context-Engine

item.title: University of Notre Dame Hosts AI Coding Assistant Security Workshop
item.description:
University of Notre Dame Hosts AI Coding Assistant Security Workshop

On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the AI Collaborative Programming group offered a virtual, hands‑on workshop where participants put AI coding assistants to the test in a web‑application security sandbox.

🔍 Overview

  • Date & Time: Thursday, October 8, 2026, 1:00 pm – 2:00 pm
  • Format: Virtual (250I Hesburgh Library link)
  • Goal: Identify and patch common security flaws using AI‑assisted tools while maintaining strict human oversight.

🛠️ Workshop Content

  • Work with AI tools such as GitHub Copilot or VS Code alongside an OWASP Juice Shop instance.
  • Follow a human‑in‑the‑loop workflow:
    • Isolate a vulnerability.
    • Create a Git branch.
    • Prompt the AI for a secure fix.
    • Verify the patch against insecure defaults.
    • Write clean PR documentation.
  • Learn to:
    • Critique AI‑generated code.
    • Spot dangerous hallucinations.
    • Maintain rigorous developer oversight.

👥 Presenters & Audience

Name Role
Rob Wieck Senior Research Software Engineer / Product Owner, AI Enablement
Julie Vecchio Interim Co‑Director, Navari Family Center for Digital Scholarship
  • Open to: Undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, staff, and postdocs.

📅 Details

  • Part of a series offered by the AI Collaborative Programming group, a partnership between Hesburgh Libraries, ND Learning, and the Office of Information Technology.
  • Location for the virtual session: 250I Hesburgh Library.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates practical ways to integrate AI coding assistants into secure software development.
  • Emphasizes the importance of human review to mitigate AI‑generated errors.
  • Provides a reproducible sandbox for learning secure coding practices.

#AI #CodingAssistants #WebSecurity #Workshop

Source: AI Masterclass: Developer Hands-On With AI-Assisted Coding Tools and OWASP Juice Shop
